# Vendored third-party source

Everything here is copied into the repository rather than fetched at build time. That is
deliberate, and it is a stronger guarantee than a fetch script: the bytes that build are
the bytes in our git history, so a fork with no network access to anywhere but GitHub —
or with no network access at all after cloning — builds exactly what we build.

`scripts/verify_third_party.sh` re-derives the tree hash below and, given network access,
compares our copy against upstream.

---

## ZIPFoundation

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | https://github.com/weichsel/ZIPFoundation |
| Version | `0.9.19` |
| Commit | `02b6abe5f6eef7e3cbd5f247c5cc24e246efcfe0` |
| Licence | MIT — `third_party/ZIPFoundation-LICENSE` |
| Vendored | 2026-08-25 |
| Location | `swift/VNPlayerCore/Sources/ZIPFoundation/` (21 `.swift` files) |
| Tree SHA-256 | `cdda661e7969435b396425f33b13430a0993d3fe1bb57c4f5cb7f67c4b84b675` |

The tree hash is over the 21 `.swift` files, sorted by name, each contributing its
basename followed by its bytes **with CRLF normalised to LF**.
`scripts/verify_third_party.sh` computes it the same way.

The normalisation is load-bearing. Git rewrites line endings on checkout depending on
platform and configuration, so a hash over raw bytes would describe the checkout rather
than the source: it would pass on the machine that generated it and fail in CI, for a
reason having nothing to do with whether the dependency had been tampered with.

### Why this and not a hand-written ZIP reader

Recorded because the first draft of the M2 spec argued the other way, and both
consultation reviewers rejected it. See
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-25-m2-library-and-import-design.md` §7.1 for the full
reasoning. Briefly: the hardening this app needs is expressed through the
consumer-closure form of `extract`, which hands us decompressed chunks and leaves the
destination decision with us — so owning the read loop bought nothing — while a
hand-rolled parser would own ZIP64 extra fields, data descriptors, and a decade of format
corner cases in the one component that parses hostile input.

### What was NOT copied

- `Package.swift` and the `Package@swift-*.swift` variants — our own package manifest
  builds these sources as a target.
- `Tests/` — upstream's tests are not run here. Ours (§11 of the M2 spec) test *our*
  extractor's behaviour, with fixtures generated by Python's `zipfile` so that an
  independent implementation produces the input.
- `Sources/ZIPFoundation/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` — an App Store privacy
  manifest. This app is sideloaded and does not submit to the App Store; if that ever
  changes, this needs to come back.

### Local modifications

**None.** These files are byte-identical to upstream at the commit above. If that ever
stops being true, say so here and say why — a silently patched dependency is how a
"pinned" version stops meaning anything.
